name: link_anim2_frame
notes: Frame index of animator slot 2 (anchor $3353). $0A at mode init (07:405A); then $0A or $0E by D5F5 (07:40B3/40CD, 07:4292/42B2); $12 = confirmed pose (07:41ED, only when D5F5=1); stepped and written back by 07:42FC-430B. Read as a test at 07:424D (cp $12).

name: link_anim3_frame
notes: Same for slot 3 (anchor $6D52). Init $0C (07:405F); $10 or $0C by D5F5 (07:40B8/40D2, 07:4297/42B7); $15 = confirmed pose (07:41DB, only when D5F5=0); stepped at 07:4312-4321; tested at 07:4237 (cp $15).

name: link_bar_x
type: u8 (B argument = X of the sprite call)
notes: X position of the first bar sprite (Y = $24, sprite $A8+DA04); the second bar sprite is at X = $A0 - DA02, Y = $54 (07:49F7-4A13). 07:49C3 increments it while DA04=0 and decrements it while DA04=1, once per frame. Cleared at 07:44F9 and 07:464A (state entry). The OAM byte order (Y first, then X) was checked in the sprite helper 00:24CB-24DA, where C is added to the first OAM byte (Y) and B to the second (X).

name: link_bar_phase
notes: Frame counter of the bar animation, wraps at $38 (07:49D0-49D9). While it is < 8 and DA04=0 the routine writes $FFB0 := $E4 and $FFB3 := $90, otherwise $FFB0 := $1B and $FFB3 := $50 (07:49E6-49F5; two HRAM shadows described in `wram_hram`: a short flash). Cleared at 07:44FC, 07:464D.

name: link_bar_dir
status: C (values); I (which role each state has)
notes: Direction of the bars (and sprite variant: $A8 + value). :=1 in states 7 and 11 (07:459B, 07:46BE), :=0 in states 8, 12 and 16 (07:45D3, 07:472F, 07:4877). Only 07:49C3 reads it.

name: link_lamp_script
type: 2 x u8: DA05 = step, DA06 = tick
notes: Step index (DA05) and tick (DA06) into the 2-byte script 07:499E (flags, duration; FF at the end loops to step 0). 07:4906 draws lamp sprites $A5 (flag bit 2, at X=$35, Y=$8C), $A6 (bit 1, X=$65) and $A7 (bit 0, X=$95, through the flicker routine 07:4948); when the tick reaches duration it advances the step (07:4930-4944). Both cleared at 07:44FF/4502 and 07:4650/4653.

name: link_flicker
type: 2 x u8: DA07 = threshold, DA08 = accumulator
notes: Random flicker of lamp 3 (07:4948-499D). If lamp bit 0 is clear: DA08 := 0, DA07 += 8 (cap $80). If set: DA08 += 9 (cap $FF); while DA08 < DA07 the lamp stays dark and DA07 += 8; otherwise the lamp is drawn, DA08 -= $23 (floor 0) and DA07 -= (RNG & 3) + 10 (floor 0), RNG = 00:08F9. Never initialised explicitly (zero from boot/clear).

name: link_pick_count
notes: Number of selectable photos in the "choose the photo" dialog: DC55 & $7F if DC52 = 0, else DC58 (07:4CE6-4CF8). A slot S is valid iff S < DA09 (07:4F58 for the grid of 8, 07:5157 for the cursor D5D8). DC52/55/58 are in region dc00 (meaning not verified here).

name: link_cancel_latch
notes: Cleared at dialog entry (07:4C2C). When B alone is pressed ($FFA2 == 2) DC56 := $EF and DA0A := $EF (07:4D18-4D2A); with DA0A non-zero the dialog waits until the peer's DC59 equals $EF, then goes to the next state (07:4CFC-4D15). So: local cancel sent, waiting for the peer's acknowledgement.

name: link_timeout
type: u16 little endian (DA0B low, DA0C high)
notes: Watchdog of the waiting states. 07:4ACB: dec [DA0B], borrow into DA0C, returns Z when both are 0 (callers 07:45E0, 07:473C, 07:4884, 07:5196). Reloaded to $0200 (07:4568/456D state 6, 07:4705/470A state 11), $00B4 (07:46EF/46F3, 07:518B/518F). On expiry: DBCF := $0C and D5CF := $12 (07:45EA, 07:4746, 07:488E). Units are frames if the states run once per frame ($200 = 512 frames, about 8.6 s; $B4 = 180 frames, 3 s): I.

name: gap_da0d
notes: Between the link-screen variables (DA00-DA0C) and the copy-screen variables (DA0F-DA13). No proven access, no P row pointing into it. Possibly spare/padding of the allocation; no evidence either way.

name: copies_of_photo
type: u8 (binary; drawn as tens/units by repeated subtraction of 10)
notes: Copies made of the selected photo D5D8 during this visit of the screen. Cleared at the mode entry (04:46A2 state 0, 04:474D state 11) and whenever D5D8 != DA13 (04:4E5F); inc in state 14 (04:4F45) then drawn by 04:4FAF. No cap was found in the code (the two-digit drawing is valid for 0..99).

name: copied_marker_xy
notes: Position of the marker sprite: 04:4FAF copies a pair from table 04:5009 (8 pairs (X,Y) = 4B 0B / 73 0B / 23 33 / 4B 33 / 73 33 / 23 5B / 4B 5B / 73 5B, i.e. 8 positions on a grid of 3 columns (X = $23/$4B/$73) and 3 rows (Y = $0B/$33/$5B) of the album screen, index = D5D8 (+2 if D5D8 >= $1E) AND 7) into DA10/DA11 (04:4FFC/5000). 04:5019 draws it with 00:24AF (B = DA10, C = DA11) and moves it up: DA11 -= 2 at countdown $24 and $21, -= 1 at $1C (04:5025-5035). B = X and C = Y per the helper (00:24CB-24DA).

name: copied_marker_timer
notes: Marker countdown: set to $26 by 04:4FAF (04:5005), decremented every frame by 04:5019 (04:501F); the marker is drawn while it is non-zero. Cleared with DA0F at entry (04:46A5, 04:4750) and on photo change (04:4E62).

name: last_photo_seen
notes: Value of D5D8 when DA0F was last reset (04:46AB, 04:4756: := D5D8); state 12 compares D5D8 with it through HL (04:4E54-4E5D: ld hl,$da13; cp [hl]; on difference DA13 := D5D8, DA0F := 0, DA12 := 0).

name: gap_da14
notes: Between the copy-screen variables and the main-menu variables (DA16-). No proven access; DA16-DA18 are cleared one by one at 00:2EE9-2EEF, which does not include these two.

name: menu_item
type: u8 0..6 (7 only through the FF table entry)
notes: Current menu item (0-2 upper page, 3-6 lower page); moved by the D-pad handlers in 07:7260-77A6 (25 writes, mostly the constants of the next item); 07:71C5 restores D5CF from the table 07:7259 after returning from another mode; indexes 07:7804 at 07:77B6. Cleared at 00:2EE9 (main loop start).

name: menu_up_col
status: C (writes/read); I (the exact items 0/1 stand for)
notes: Remembered upper-row column (0/1): which upper-row item the player came from when moving down to item 2. Cleared at main-loop start (00:2EEC) and at menu entry (07:71DB, A = 0 from the xor a at 07:71D6); := 0 at 07:72C0 and := 1 at 07:733A when Down is pressed (item 1 -> item 2, DA16 := 2); read by the state of item 2 (07:73E7) to choose which upper-row item Up returns to.

name: menu_sel_upper
notes: Upper-page item from which Select was pressed (07:72E6 := 0, 07:7357 := 1, 07:7390 := 2; read at 07:7775). Cleared at 00:2EEF.

name: menu_sel_lower
notes: Lower-page item from which Select was pressed (07:754A, 07:75F3, 07:769C, 07:7745; read at 07:7437).

name: menu_anim_tick[5]
notes: Tick of each icon animator, incremented by the callback stubs (07:7B25-7B42); proven reads only in the page set-up code (07:7947, 07:79A7: icon 0 tick == 1 triggers the tile-block copy to $8000/$8100). [Update: the callbacks 07:7AF1-7B43 and the transition helpers 07:7BF4-7D30 are reached through the tables at 07:7985-7AD3 and are now proven live by the v3 trace (tools/extra_roots.json), so these accesses are on live code. What the bytes mean on screen stays an inference. Earlier status: I (writes only in the unproven callbacks)]

name: menu_anim_frame[5]
type: 5 x u8, index into 07:7B44 (2-byte entries sprite, duration; FF = loop target in the next byte)
notes: Frame of each icon animator, clamped by 07:7900, stepped by the callbacks. In the set-up code the first icon's frame selects which of three tile blocks is copied to VRAM (07:794D: frames $39 / $3B and others 07:7950-797E; 07:79AD: $3E / $40). [Update: the callbacks 07:7AF1-7B43 and the transition helpers 07:7BF4-7D30 are reached through the tables at 07:7985-7AD3 and are now proven live by the v3 trace (tools/extra_roots.json), so these accesses are on live code. What the bytes mean on screen stays an inference. Earlier status: I (writes in the unproven callbacks; clamp write `07:7900-790F` is proven)]

name: menu_anim_y[5]
notes: Y of each icon (ld c,[DA24+i] at 07:7B1D-7B21), loaded by 07:7900 from byte 2 of the 6-byte entry (07:7919). Values e.g. $29, $14, $5F on the upper page. [Update: the callbacks 07:7AF1-7B43 and the transition helpers 07:7BF4-7D30 are reached through the tables at 07:7985-7AD3 and are now proven live by the v3 trace (tools/extra_roots.json), so these accesses are on live code. What the bytes mean on screen stays an inference. Earlier status: I (the loads/uses are in hand-decoded code; OAM order checked at `00:24CB`)]

name: menu_anim_x[5]
notes: X of each icon (ld b,[DA29+i] at 07:7B18-7B1C), loaded from byte 3 of the entry (07:7922). Values e.g. $8D, $64, $7C. [Update: the callbacks 07:7AF1-7B43 and the transition helpers 07:7BF4-7D30 are reached through the tables at 07:7985-7AD3 and are now proven live by the v3 trace (tools/extra_roots.json), so these accesses are on live code. What the bytes mean on screen stays an inference. Earlier status: I (as above)]

name: menu_trans_stamp
notes: Frame-pacing stamp of the four-step page transition routines 07:7BDC, 07:7C4C, 07:7CBB (entered with HL = a draw callback and DE = a table of 3-byte (addr, bank) entries, e.g. 07:7C27; each step copies a 512-byte tile block from that table to VRAM $9100 through 00:05F8, runs the callback, 07:7BEC-7C18): each step stores $FFC8 here (07:7BE9, 07:7C58, 07:7CC7; proven writes). The reader is 07:7D14 (hand-decoded: a := DA2E - $FFC8 + 4, then the step callback is run that many more frames), so each step lasts about 4 frames in total. [Update: the callbacks 07:7AF1-7B43 and the transition helpers 07:7BF4-7D30 are reached through the tables at 07:7985-7AD3 and are now proven live by the v3 trace (tools/extra_roots.json), so these accesses are on live code. What the bytes mean on screen stays an inference. Earlier status: I (reader only in hand-decoded code)]

name: menu_item3_phase
status: C (counter); I (what the tile blocks show)
notes: Phase counter of an icon animation of the lower page (07:79F7: +1 mod $28); at phases $18, $20, $26 the 512-byte tile block $15:4E00 is copied to VRAM $8300 (07:7A1C-7A27), at phases 0, $1C, $24 the block $15:5000 (07:7A2C-7A37), then the lower-page animators are run (07:7A3F). Bank number $15 is hexadecimal. Wrapped to 0 at 07:79FF-7A00.

name: menu_state_copy
notes: Menu state at the moment A/B/Start was pressed (07:726F and six more write sites, one per page position); read only at 07:77CC, which restores D5CF from it when the mode byte of the chosen item is >= $22 (the FF entry).

name: edge_dir
type: u8 bit mask ($10 right, $20 left, $40 up, $80 down: the D-pad bits of $FFA2)
notes: Direction in which the cursor was clamped this frame. Cleared every frame at the top of the cursor routine (04:5D93, 04:646C), set by the clamp code (04:5E1B/5E29, 04:655C/656A), read at 04:5C64, 04:61A7 (P rows 04:5C55, 04:6198 are ld hl,$da31).

name: edge_count
notes: Number of consecutive frames the pressed direction equals DA31: incremented/cleared at 04:5C5B/5C6E and 04:619E/61B1, tested at 04:5C6A, 04:61AD. At >= 10 frames the mode goes to its state 3 (04:5C75-5C97, 04:66DB). The exact label of state 3 (options panel?) is not verified here.

name: deco_tick[4]
notes: Tick counters of four decorative sprites. 09:5219: for each pair i, tick+1; if < limit[i] store, else tick := 0 and phase[i] := (phase[i] + 1) AND 3. Limits (table 09:5269) = 0D 10 07 17 (13, 16, 7, 23 frames).

name: deco_phase[4]
notes: Phase of the four sprites, drawn at fixed positions BC = $4550, $7049, $6D6C, $9177 with sprite ids $61 + DA37, $65 + (DA38 & 1), $6B + DA39, $67 + DA3A (09:523A-5265, 00:247D).

name: kb_cursor
notes: Character position being edited in the field (name buffer DA4D + cursor, or the 8 date digits). Cleared at state 6 entry (09:4B12); 15 reads and 16 writes in 09:57F3-5F2A (arrows, typing, delete).

name: kb_key
status: C (data flow); I (labels of special keys)
notes: Key under the keyboard cursor. Gender: keys 0..2 are stored directly in DA56 bits 0-1 (09:5D3B-5D44); blood type: keys 0..5 are accepted (09:5EA7) and stored shifted left twice into DA56 bits 2-4 (09:5EB2-5EBA); thresholds $3E/$41/$44/$47/$4A/$4D on this value select the special keys on the character pages (delete, left, right, confirm...: exact labels I).

name: kb_page
notes: Keyboard/tab page: 0..2 = character pages (pointer table 09:5C0E), 3 = confirm page, 4 = birth-date page, 5 = blood-type page; written when a tab is selected (09:5C3F, 09:5C54, 09:5C69: := 0, 1, 2).

name: kb_tab_tick[3]
notes: Tick of the 'tab pressed' animation of tab C = 0..2 (09:5881: add hl,bc).

name: kb_tab_frame[3]
notes: Frame of the tab animation: 0 = idle, set to 1 when the tab is selected (09:5C3B, 09:5C4F, 09:5C64), then stepped by 09:5881 through table 09:58B4 = (variant,duration) pairs 00 04, 00 04, 01 04, 00 03, 01 03, 00 02, 01 02 and back to 0 at 7 (blink with shortening period). Cleared at state 6 entry (09:4B1B/4B1E/4B21). The returned variant bit chooses the sprite.

name: shoot_fx_vector[5]
notes: Block-copied by 06:6C54 (P row 06:6C61), then read byte-wise: DA44/DA45 at 06:7484/7488, 06:7591/7595, 06:76C2/76C6; DA46/DA47 at 06:74C7/74CB, 06:75E0/75E4, 06:7711/7715; DA48 at 06:752E, 06:7653, 06:7784. Each is used as a mask applied to tile-row bytes of the work image $C000: the data flow is solid, but what each of the six effects looks like on screen was not decoded.

name: owner_id
notes: Owner ID number (8 digits). Accessed only as a block (02:5054 load, 02:4BF4 save, 02:46F0) and by the draw/edit routines of bank 9 through HL.

name: owner_name
notes: Owner name, 9 characters, edited with cursor DA3B. Drawn by 09:49B9, 09:54BC/54D5, edited at 09:5BF3, 09:5CA1, 09:5F24 (all through HL).

name: owner_gender_blood
type: u8: bits 0-1 gender key (0..2), bits 2-4 blood-type key
notes: Written by 09:5D44 (and $FC then or key) and 09:5EBA (key<<2 or gender). Bit 0 and bit 1 are used as two independent flags elsewhere: 02:462F adds 1 (cap 99) to $CF12 if bit 0, to $CF13 if bit 1, and always to $CF14 of the received photo's tag (both tag copies: two passes of the loop at 02:465E-46B3, the second at +$5C, each followed by the checksum 02:432F over $5A bytes); 07:4A17 adds 1 to $DA9E / $DA9F for bit 0 / bit 1 of the *sender's* byte, which arrives in $CFFF (07:4409/07:477D copy DA56 there). README §3.3 codes the field as 0 none / 1 male / 2 female; no instruction states which key or bit is which gender, so the naming stays I.

name: owner_birth_year
notes: Birth year.

name: owner_birth_month
notes: Birth month.

name: owner_birth_day
notes: Birth day.

name: tag_owner_id
notes: ID of the camera owner that took the photo. Only block-copied (02:4979, 02:4E7E, 02:4EA2); no proven instruction reads a byte of it.

name: tag_owner_name
notes: Name of the owner of the camera that took the photo; drawn by 09:47B6 through HL.

name: tag_gender_blood
type: u8 (SRAM F0D): bits 0-1 gender, bits 2-4 blood type
notes: Same layout as DA56. 09:463F takes bits 0-1 and picks a 64-byte picture from 09:56D0 (4 pictures, copied to VRAM $8B80); 09:465F takes bits 2-4 and picks one from 09:54E0 (8 pictures, to $9450).

name: tag_birth
type: 4 bytes (SRAM F0E-F11): year (2 bytes), month, day
notes: Birth date of the camera owner; 09:4687 draws year (DA69, 2 bytes), month (DA6B), day (DA6C) with 09:46A5, which draws a placeholder when all bytes of the field are 0.

name: tag_count_a
notes: Reception counter bumped by 02:462F when the receiver's DA56 has bit 0 set (cap 99); drawn as two digits by 09:46C6 (DA6D, then DA6E).

name: tag_count_b
notes: Same for bit 1 (02:4674).

name: tag_count_total
notes: Bumped on every reception (02:467E-4684); drawn by 09:4706.

name: tag_comment
type: 27 x u8 (SRAM F15-F2F), chars = grid code + 1, 0 = blank
notes: Comment text, 27 editable cells (cursor DA91 is limited to $1A); drawn by 09:461E (B = $1E: it draws 30 cells, the last three are the next row), edited by 09:4281-45FF, all through HL.

name: tag_comment_tail
notes: Three bytes after the 27 comment cells. README §3.3 records them as 00 except in three 1A-filled slots of one save; no proven instruction names them, the comment drawing routine 09:461E covers them (30 cells) and the editor never moves the cursor onto them.

name: tag_copy_flag
notes: Read by 09:471B/4728 (digit tile set of the counters) and 09:474D (chooses tile data $5870 vs $5790 for VRAM $92B0), i.e. it changes how the card is drawn. No proven instruction writes it in WRAM: it comes with the loaded tag. README §3.3 documents it as the *copy flag* (01 = created by the album Copy function, set by 02:45A1 in both SRAM tag copies); I did not re-verify that writer.

name: tag_image_check
notes: Two 8-bit checksums of the 3584-byte image $C000-$CDFF: DA8F = additive sum (02:4005-402E, add a,[hl] over $E00 bytes), DA90 = XOR (02:4031-405A), computed just before a shot is saved, stored into the new tag ($CF34/$CF35, 02:4755/4759) and re-read by 00:16F4, which splits both bytes into four nibbles in $DD03-$DD06 and plays sound $10 through 00:2A7C. 00:16F4 is called after saving a shot (06:514C, 06:53AE, 06:639A, 06:63C6, 06:6404) and from the album viewer (07:717B, after 02:4E5F).

name: cmt_cursor
notes: Position of the text cursor in the comment (limit $1A, 09:4435-4462); 8 reads / 4 writes in 09:42A6-4474, 09:45EB/45F7.

name: cmt_grid_cell
notes: Cell of the character grid under the cursor (grid of 5 columns: 09:4409, 09:44A3, 09:4531, 09:4558, 09:4582).

name: cmt_ctrl
notes: Selected control: 0 = grid, 1 = delete, 2 = left arrow, 3 = right arrow (table 09:43EB; 09:43DB, 09:449A, 09:44F8).

name: cmt_grid_row
notes: Scroll row of the character grid: 09:4866 copies $A0 * page bytes from bank $2A $4000 to VRAM $8E60.

name: cmt_photo_index
notes: Photo whose tag is edited/displayed. Written by 04:6DA2, 04:7B6C (from D5EE/D5ED) and 08:46AA (print info page); read by 09:4778, which shows index - $1E + 1 for album B.

name: cnt_taken
notes: Photos taken: +1 BCD (00:0F9C, B=2) by 06:7823; read by 09:5317 (statistics screen 09:530E) and 02:4D13/4D19 (unlock test). Saved by 02:4BB2 (P 02:4BC8), loaded by 02:503F (P 02:5046).

name: cnt_erased
notes: Photos erased: 04:50E5 loads the block (02:503F), adds 1 in BCD with 00:0F9C (ld hl,$da98, B=2, 04:50F1-50F6) and saves it with 02:4BB2; read by 09:5320/5326.

name: cnt_sent
notes: Photos transferred: incremented by 07:4ADA (P 07:4AE6), called from 07:4603 (state 9) and 07:48A7 (state 17); read by 09:532F/5335, 02:4D31/4D37.

name: cnt_printed
notes: Photos printed: incremented by 00:354D (P 00:3559) when the last page of a job is done (00:33DC state 6 with DBC5); read by 09:534E/5354, 02:4D22/4D28.

name: cnt_recv_a
notes: Photos received from a camera whose owner byte has bit 0: 07:4A17 (P 07:4A21), called from 07:460C, 07:48B0; reads $CFFF bit 0, cap $99. Read by 09:533E.

name: cnt_recv_b
notes: Same for bit 1; read by 09:5345.

name: best_shooter
notes: Best score of the mode-$07 shooter (called "Space Fever II" in the manual; I). 07:6797 compares the current score $D868-$D86B with it (P 07:679A, 07:67AD) and copies it on a new record, saved by 02:4BB2 from 07:56D7, 07:56F5, 07:5713, 07:591E. Read by 09:5375-5387 (statistics), by 02:4D40-4D49 (unlock test) and by the shooter's start code 07:59F9-5A0E, which sets D831 := $40 when the stored best is below 2000 (DAA3 = DAA2 = 0 and DAA1 < $20).

name: best_ball
notes: Best score of mode $20 (05:74CC; the "Ball" game, I): 05:7E89 compares $D9E6/$D9E7 through HL (P 05:7E8C, 05:7E9F) and saves with 02:4BB2. Read by 09:5390/5396, 04:5827 (caps DAA5 to 5 for $D642), 02:4D58 (unlock).

name: best_run
type: u16 (10CB-10CC): DAA7 = first digit pair, DAA6 = second pair, stored as the nine's complement of the displayed digits
status: C (flow and complement display); I (game name, time reading)
notes: Best result of mode $21 (09:5FE3; the "Run! Run! Run!" game, I). 09:5372-53AD displays DAA7 then DAA6 as $99 - byte (cpl; add a,$9A), so a cleared block reads 99 99; written by 09:725E, which computes $99 - [$D029] (09:7266-7268) and $99 - [$D028] (09:727C-727E), compares high byte first against DAA7/DAA6 and copies only if the new complement is larger (09:726A-726C; P 09:7261, 09:7277), then 02:4BB2 saves. So the game result in $D029:$D028 (BCD, $D029 high) is better when *smaller*, and a smaller displayed number is the better result: 02:4D67 unlocks bit 7 when the stored DAA7 >= $82 (displayed <= 17), and state 18 (09:4CFC-4D0B) takes the second scene when the stored word is >= $7799 (displayed <= 22 00). Whether the number is a time is not stated by the code (I).

name: stats_spare
notes: No proven instruction touches them individually; they only travel with the block copy of 02:503F/02:4BB2.

name: print_intensity
notes: Printer density: changed by Left/Right in the print options (08:4441, cap $7F, sound $22; W 08:4457), saved on exit by 08:4427, read by 00:1BDB into $DC34 (4th data byte of the PRNT packet, $DC2D block). Loaded by 02:503F like the rest.

name: del_cx[16]
notes: Centre X of the swirl: all 16 entries = high byte of the word at 04:519D + 2*(D5D8 & 7) (04:5121-513D); added to the X offset in 04:5275-527E.

name: del_cy[16]
notes: Centre Y: all 16 entries = low byte of the same word (04:5133); added to the Y offset in 04:5295-529E.

name: del_x[16]
notes: Current X of each sprite, written to OAM byte 1 (04:5326-532B). Phase 1: H(radius x trig(angle)) + DAAC[e] (04:527A); phase 2: += DB0C[e] unless X is in $A4..$FB (04:52C9-52DB).

name: del_y[16]
notes: Current Y minus 8; OAM byte 0 = value + 8 (04:531D-5324). Phase 1 at 04:529A; phase 2: += DB1C[e] unless Y is in $94..$FB (04:52EC-52FB).

name: del_angle[16]
status: C (use); I (angle units: a full turn of 256 is assumed from the `$3F`-masked quarter-wave table)
notes: Angle of each sprite, += 2 per phase-1 frame (04:522D-5236). Initial values (04:51CD) = A0 B3 CD E0 8D A0 E0 F3 73 60 20 0D 60 4D 33 20.

name: del_radius[16]
notes: Radius, decremented to 0 once per phase-1 frame (04:5238-5246); initial values 11 0C 0C 11 0C 08 08 0C 0C 08 08 0C 11 0C 0C 11 (17, 12 or 8 frames of spiral). All zero -> phase 1 done.

name: del_vel[2][16]
type: 32 x s8: DB0C-DB1B = X velocity, DB1C-DB2B = Y velocity
notes: Initial X velocities FC FE 02 04 repeated 4 times, initial Y velocities F8 F8 F8 F8 FC FC FC FC FE FE FE FE FF FF FF FF (all negative). += acceleration each phase-2 step (04:52B6-52C4, 32 bytes), then added to the position.

name: del_acc[2][16]
type: 32 x s8: DB2C-DB3B = X acceleration, DB3C-DB4B = Y acceleration
notes: Initial values: X acceleration 0 (16 x 00), Y acceleration 2 (16 x 02): a downward pull, so the burst falls back.

name: del_done
notes: Phase-finished flag: cleared at 04:516A (before phase 1) and 04:5185 (before phase 2), set at 04:524E (all radii 0), 04:52E6 and 04:5303 (X and Y loops of phase 2); read at 04:517E, 04:5196 as the loop exits.

name: print_src_table[4]
type: 4 entries x 4 bytes (lo, hi, bank, pad)
notes: Sources of band data. Entry 0 = the photo address given by 02:517B (A=bank, B=hi, C=lo), stored at 08:4617-461F, 08:4663-466B, 08:4750-475A (info page: $C000, bank 0) and 08:4AE6-4AEE; 08:540D fills entries 1..3 (DB51/DB55/DB59: three consecutive 2 KiB graphic chunks, hi += 8 each, wrapping to the next bank via table 08:54C6); 06:5AE0 fills entries 3..0 for a 4-photo SHOOT job (06:5AE3; an absent photo = FF FF FF, zero-filled by 00:3214). Read by 00:31E2 with index = descriptor flags & 3 (P 00:3178).

name: print_src_table2[4]
notes: Second table. The only proven writer is 08:50F6/08:5106 (DB61, the first triple of the border graphics table 08:511F, 6 bytes per border number D7C1; the second triple goes to DB51). The base DB5D is loaded at 00:31A5 (reader through HL, selected by descriptor bit 5?). Entries 0, 2 and 3 are never written by proven code.

name: print_layout_type
notes: Page layout: 0 plain (08:462D), 1 framed (08:467A), 4 info page (08:475F), 08:4B09 := 0, 06:5B22 := ($D5EA xor 1) + 2 (2 or 3, the 4-photo layouts). Read at 00:30DD (table 00:30F9) and 00:311B (table 00:32E8).

name: print_return_idx
notes: Return-target index: table 00:3483 = 1C 08, 1C 08, 18 00, 18 00, 1E 05 (mode, state) used when the job ends (00:346E). Written by 08:4630, 08:467D, 08:4763, 08:4B0E (:= 4), 06:5B25.

name: print_pages
notes: Number of pages of the job (08:4637, 08:4684, 08:4771, 08:4B16, 06:5B18); 00:3321: after DBC3 is incremented, equality with DB6F sets DBC5 := 1 (last page).

name: print_band_desc[40]
notes: Band descriptors, copied from bank 8 by 00:3214; rendered by 00:3161 (P 00:3136, 00:3161) into $CF00. Flags: bits 0-1 source entry, bit 3 -> DBC5 := 1 (00:31C4), bit 4 -> 1bpp expansion (00:3249), bit 5 -> indirect/second source (purpose not proven), bit 6 -> blank tile, bit 7 -> DBC6 := 1 (00:3188).

name: print_script_off
notes: Byte offset into the layout script (+$50 per band; read 00:312A/312E, advanced 00:3144/3148). Cleared at 00:3035/3038.

name: print_band_no
notes: Band counter of the current page: cleared at 00:30C9 (state 00:30AB, run once per page after the printer answered with $81 in $DC28), incremented through HL once per band (P 00:314E, 00:3151); when it reaches 9 DBC6 := 1 (00:3153-3159). 9 bands x 2 tile rows = the 18 tile rows (144 lines) of one image.

name: print_page_no
notes: Page index: cleared 00:303B, incremented 00:3320 (P 00:331D), read 00:30E9, 00:3321.

name: print_first_page
notes: Top-margin flag: := 1 at 00:3043, := 0 at 00:33FB; read at 00:3359.

name: print_last_page
notes: Bottom-margin flag: cleared 00:3032, set by descriptor bit 3 (00:31C4) and by 00:332C; read 00:3360 (margin) and 00:33EE (triggers 00:354D).

name: print_last_band
notes: Cleared with DBC2 at the start of each page (00:30CC); set to 1 when the band counter reaches 9 (00:3159, in the band set-up 00:3118) and by descriptor bit 7 (00:3188); read 00:32F5 (copied to $DC3D) and 00:3317.

name: print_progress_step
notes: Loaded at 00:30F1/30F5 (called from 00:30D5, start of each page) from the table 00:30F9 (offset byte per layout DB6D, then one word per page index DBC3); read through HL at 00:3522.

name: print_progress_acc
notes: Accumulator: cleared 00:30CF/30D2 at the start of each page, advanced by the step at 00:3515-3522; (hi >> 3) capped at 15 selects $54DE + 5*a for call $0A8A (progress picture).

name: print_layout_flag
notes: Cleared at 08:412B, 04:6C80, 04:79E9, 08:47B6 (state 11, after 02:48F7); set to 1 at 08:47E7 (state 14); read at 08:4218 (0 = plain path, loads the photo with 02:4E31/02:517B; non-zero = framed path 08:424D), 08:4602 (after D803 is incremented), 08:480C. This is the flag the previous README meant by "the shared flag $dbcb" that chooses between the two layout templates.

name: border_normalised
notes: Latch so that a border number $D7C1 == $12 is normalised only once: in the plain-layout path (DBCB = 0) 08:4231-423E replaces $D7C1 by 0 and sets this latch to 1 (same in 08:4832); read at 08:421E, 08:4812; cleared at 04:6C83, 04:79EC, 08:412E.

name: del_variant
notes: := 0 in state 9 (04:4C8E, single photo), := 1 in state 10 (04:4D78, erase all); read at 04:5153 (sound $3B vs $05) and 04:52AB (phase 2 every frame vs every other frame).

name: link_setup_done
notes: Cleared at mode init (07:40A5), set to 1 in the first frame of state 1 which then runs 00:2D5F once (07:410E-4118, 07:4115).

name: result_msg_id
status: C (flow); ? (the texts and which printer condition each status bit is)
notes: Message id of the shared result/error screen 09:7290, which looks it up in the table 09:739E (3 bytes per entry) -> text tiles $8900; id $0E forces picture set 3, otherwise a random set 0..2 (09:7346). Writers: 00:343B (printer status mapping: bit 7 -> 0, bit 6 -> 3, bit 5 -> 2, otherwise 1), 03:62FA := 6, 04:71BD/71C9/71FA := 0E/04/08, 06:53FB := 9, 06:726F := 0D, 07:417D (from $DC50 through the table 07:4186 = 09 09 0A 0B), 07:45EA/4746/488E := 0C, 07:7122 := 5. Readers: 04:71E0, 09:7346, 09:737F.

name: printer_prev_status
notes: At every received printer byte 00:18BD-18D2: DBD1 := [$DC27] (previous reply byte, 00:18C6) and DBD0 := [$DC27] unless it is $FF (00:18CD); then $DC27 := [$FF01]. Never read by any proven instruction.

name: gap_dbd2
notes: After the two write-only printer status bytes (DBD0/DBD1) and before the DBEC table. No proven access and no P row inside; the DBEC table (9 x u16, row above) ends at DBFD, so this gap is also not part of it.

name: printer_len_table
status: U (dead path; no proven writer of `DC0B` or of the table)
notes: Packet-length table of 00:19EB: bc := [DBEC + 2*(DC3E-2)] (00:1A3D, 00:1AA0), used only when $DC0B != 0. DC0B has no proven writer (only reads at 00:1A1B, 00:1A7E), so the default bc := $0280 is always taken. The size 18 is only the distance to DBFE.

name: printer_dc0c_table
type: bytes indexed by DC3E-2; extends into $DC00 (dc00 region)
notes: Feeds $DC0C (00:1A2E, 00:1A91) in the same dead path. Only the first 2 bytes are in my range.
